body: I think this was changed in #25879 and seems like an intentional change (a fix).
@gkalpak yep, but there is no `comment nodes`, it's regular nodes and they are removed. Looks like breaking change

I don't know the details (just stating the facts (that it was changed in #25879 and seems intentional).
@mhevery or @IgorMinar should know more (including whether this qualifies as a breaking change or not and why) :grin:

Yes this was intentional change. The reason we remove the unknown elements is that they could be web-components which would allow user to trigger code, and could provide security hole.

So this works as intended.
@mhevery but there is nothing in changelog about this change and it's really is breaking one cause breaks previous behavior

https://angular.io/guide/releases
> Minor releases are fully backward-compatible; no developer assistance is expected during update

i've simply updated an app from 7.0.3 to 7.2.2 and this suddenly breaks part of our major functional (expected sanitized text became empty).
Just to be clear: i want to rely on angular versioning without testing everything on minor update and guessing what breaks it (nothing in changelog about this, only about comments removing)

> i've simply updated an app from 7.0.3 to 7.2.2 and this suddenly breaks part of our major functional (expected sanitized text became empty).
> Just to be clear: i want to rely on angular versioning without testing everything on minor update and guessing what breaks it (nothing in changelog about this, only about comments removing)

Yes, you are right, we should have done a better job communicating, and we are sorry. Normally we have these higher risk items in major versions only, but because this one had security implications it was included in the patch release.

Ohh, I see. You are right there is no reason to remove the content. The reason we remove the content is if there is `<style>` we remove style and hence it's content. But we should not do that for everything, only for a waitlisted set of elements. 

Would you be willing to create a PR for this?
